Michigan.what_qualifies: up to 3 felonies and unlimited misdemeanors (most nonviolent offenses)

Minnesota.lawyer_allowed: generally no, unless the judge allows it
Minnesota.what_qualifies: dismissed cases; misdemeanors, gross misdemeanors, and listed felonies; some automatic under Clean Slate

Mississippi.waiting_period: varies — immediate for non-convictions; up to 15 years for felonies
Mississippi.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted cases; first-offense misdemeanors; up to 3 felonies after 15 years

Missouri.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors and non-Class-A felonies (violent/sex/DWI excluded)

Montana.available: very limited — no adult felony expungement
Montana.lawyer_allowed: no, unless all parties have one
Montana.what_qualifies: misdemeanors once per lifetime; dismissed deferred sentences

Nebraska.available: very limited — no expungement of adult convictions
Nebraska.waiting_period: varies — 1–3 years for sealing non-conviction records
Nebraska.what_qualifies: sealing for arrests/charges with no conviction; set-aside for probation/fine sentences

Nevada.lawyer_allowed: yes, but attorney's fees can't be awarded
Nevada.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors and felonies; sex crimes/child crimes/felony DUI excluded

New Hampshire.what_qualifies: most violations, misdemeanors, and felonies except certain violent/sexual offenses

New Jersey.waiting_period: 5 years (most offenses); 10 years for automatic Clean Slate
New Jersey.what_qualifies: most indictable offenses (limited number), disorderly persons offenses, municipal ordinances
